findings.title: The 503/terminal:false fix for uploadStatus never reaches the poll loop: the generic fetch wrapper throws on any non-2xx response before 'terminal' can be read
findings.suggested_fix: In client.js's handle(), a 503 response still fails response.ok, so appAPI.uploadStatus() rejects with an ApiError; _await's catch block (line 135-137) treats every rejection as terminal and ends the poll loop with an error message, exactly the pre-fix behavior for a 500. The server-side StorageUnreachable -> 503 + {terminal:false} change (controllers.uploadStatus, controllers.py ~line 424-441) is dead code from the client's perspective. Fix by having the catch block inspect error.status (e.g. continue polling on 503/ApiError with status 503, or have uploadStatus's rejection carry the parsed body so terminal can be checked) instead of unconditionally ending the loop on any thrown error.

findings.title: Staleness detection has no heartbeat during long single stages (esp. 'converting'), so a genuinely slow but successful conversion can be reported FAILED to a polling client that then stops watching
findings.suggested_fix: progress() in management/commands/ingest_archive.py is only invoked at stage transitions (extracting/converting/describing/publishing/done); convert_outputs.py runs the whole consolidation as one blocking pass with no interim progress calls. If a large run's 'converting' stage runs longer than STALE_AFTER_SECONDS (default 30 min) without a status write, _fail_if_stale synthesizes a terminal FAILED on the next poll even though the subprocess is still alive and later writes DONE; the client's poll loop (ngiab-upload-run.js _await) stops on the first terminal response, so the user is told the upload failed while the run is silently published moments later. Add a periodic heartbeat write (e.g. every few minutes) inside long stages, or have the controller's in-process _running/_reap machinery corroborate staleness with actual process liveness before declaring failure.

findings.title: Batched S3 delete_objects sets Quiet=True and never inspects the response's Errors array, so a partial deletion failure is silently treated as success
findings.suggested_fix: delete_objects can return per-object errors (permission denied, object lock, etc.) even on a 200 response; with Quiet=True those are never surfaced, and the code does not check response.get('Errors'). This path is used both by run_store.delete() (user-triggered, irreversible run removal) and by ingest._upload_directory's cleanup-on-failed-publish. A partial failure leaves orphaned objects in the bucket indefinitely while callers believe the prefix is fully removed. Set Quiet=False (or inspect the Errors list) and raise/log when any deletions failed.

findings.title: Check-then-act race on the concurrency bound: _reap() count check and _running.append() are not atomic
findings.suggested_fix: _launch() reads _reap() >= MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS, then appends to _running several lines later with no lock. Two upload requests handled concurrently (sync views run through a thread pool under ASGI) can both observe a count under the limit and both proceed, briefly exceeding MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS by the number of racing requests. Guard the check-and-append with a threading.Lock around _reap()+append in _launch().

residual_risks: controllers._reap() only runs as a side effect of launching a new ingest (_launch). If no further upload is attempted after the last child exits, that child remains an unreaped zombie process-table entry for the remaining life of the worker; harmless in isolation (bounded by MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS=2, cleared on worker exit) but the claim that zombies are 'closed' is really 'reaped lazily on next use', not eliminated.

ingest._workspace() stages local ingests under <storage-root>/_uploads (or /tmp on object storage) and relies on publish()'s `finally: shutil.rmtree(...)` to clean up; a SIGKILL (the OOM scenario this commit explicitly designs the staleness fix around) skips that finally, leaving a half-populated workspace directory on disk permanently with no sweep to reclaim it. This is not new (the previous /tmp-based workspace had the same gap), but relocating it under the storage root means orphaned ingest debris now competes for space on the same volume that holds published runs rather than system /tmp.

duckdb_conn._with_fresh_credentials classifies retryable auth failures by matching lowercase substrings ('access denied', 'http 403', etc.) in the exception message. A non-auth error that happens to contain 'access denied' (e.g. a bucket policy or VPC-endpoint restriction unrelated to credential rotation) would trigger a pointless reset()+retry; because the retry is bounded to one attempt this does not create a storm, only a wasted round trip, so it is not flagged as a hard finding.
testing_gaps: No test exercises the real HTTP path for uploadStatus's 503 response through client.js's handle()/fetch wrapper; ngiab-upload-run.test.js stubs appAPI.uploadStatus directly with plain objects, so the test suite cannot detect that a genuine 503 becomes a thrown ApiError that _await treats as terminal, masking the ineffective fix described above.

No test drives a job through _fail_if_stale returning a synthetic FAILED and then later observes the underlying status object actually resolving to DONE (i.e. the 'client gave up on a job that then succeeded' scenario) end to end through uploadStatus + the JS poll loop.
No test exercises delete_objects returning a non-empty Errors array in the Quiet=True batched-delete path to confirm partial failures surface rather than being swallowed.
